podcast.title: Evolution from Southern Death Cult
podcast.body: The band was initially known as Southern Death Cult, then became Death Cult, and by 1985, they were simply The Cult, showing a progression in their identity. "First they were Southern death cult. Then they became just death cult. By 1985 they were just the cults"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Astbury's Band (1983-1984)
xref.body: An Ian Astbury-led band mentioned as one of the many groups contributing to the expanding goth scene in the 1983-1984 period. It later evolved into Death Cult and then The Cult. "In Asperg band, Southern Death Cult."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Name Evolution
xref.body: Before settling on "The Cult," the band went by two other names: Southern Death Cult (for one album) and Death Cult (for another). By the end of 1983, they were simply "The Cult." "Up until that record came out, The Cult went by two other names."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Goth Origins
xref.body: Southern Death Cult began their career as a Goth band. "They began as a Goth band and my hang on, I'll explain in a second."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Later Commercial Success
xref.body: After their evolution from Southern Death Cult and Death Cult, The Cult achieved significant commercial success, selling millions of records in the late 1980s and early 1990s. "And yes, it is the cult that went on to sell millions of records in the late 80s and early 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Name Evolution
xref.body: The band underwent a name change, first shortening it to Death Cult, and then eventually becoming The Cult. "They started pretty Goth, then they shortened their name to just Death Cult. And finally they just became the cult."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tours with Bauhaus
xref.body: Southern Death Cult frequently toured with Bauhaus. "It's a band called Southern Death Cult, who often toured with Bauhaus and featured a singer who spent much of his time growing up in Southern Ontario."
